topics.description: An Abadan movie theater destroyed by a devastating 1978 fire that became a major flashpoint preceding the Iranian Revolution.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer some questions about the SAVAK secret police force:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] SAVAK was active in this country until its 1979 revolution, which saw the overthrow of its Shah Mohammad Reza Pahlavi. More than 50 Americans were held hostage in this country’s city of Tehran.
parts.answer: Iran [or Islamic Republic of Iran or Jomhuri-ye Eslami-ye Iran; accept Iranian Revolution]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] After SAVAK’s dissolution, many of its members became members of SAVAMA, an intelligence agency under this ruler. This first supreme leader of Iran took power in the Iranian Revolution.
parts.answer: Ayatollah Khomeini [or Ruhollah Khomeini or Sayyid Ruhollah Musavi Khomeini; prompt on Ayatollah; reject “Khamenei”]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] A large 1978 fire in the “Rex” one of these places may have been intentionally set by the SAVAK secret police. Swedish Prime Minister Olof Palme was assassinated while walking home from one of these places.
parts.answer: cinemas [or movie theaters or the movies; accept Cinema Rex; accept Grand Cinema]

topics.description: The German king and Holy Roman Emperor who defeated the Magyars at Lechfeld and was crowned emperor in 962.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A king of these people was crowned by Pope Sylvester II on Christmas Day, 1000. For 10 points  each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name these people who were ruled by Árpád (AR-pod) and Saint Stephen I. Their kingdom entered  a “dual monarchy” with Austria 867 years later.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Magyars' western expansion was ended at the 955 Battle of Lechfeld (LESH-feld) by this  “Great” Holy Roman Emperor, who was crowned in 962 and was the son of Henry the Fowler.
parts.answer: Otto I [or Otto the Great; prompt on Otto]

parts.label: C
parts.question: After settling in the Carpathian Basin, Magyars fought with people from this present-day country,  who were shortly thereafter slain at the Battle of Kleidion (KLEE-dee-ahn) by Byzantine emperor Basil  II.
parts.answer: Bulgaria [Republic of Bulgaria; or Republika Bulgaria]

topics.description: The Great Leap Forward was Mao Zedong's campaign to rapidly industrialize and collectivize China, resulting in catastrophic famine from 1959 to 1961.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This leader denounced the Five Black Categories, which included “rich peasants” and “rightists.” This leader began political campaigns with photoshoots of himself crossing a river. This leader temporarily encouraged criticism in the Hundred Flowers Movement, and caused a famine attempting to eradicate (*) sparrows in the Four Pests campaign. This leader promoted steel-making communes in the Great Leap Forward. This leader oversaw the Cultural Revolution and published many of his writings in The Little Red Book. For 10 points, name this former Chairman of the People’s Republic of China.

topics.description: An international organization established in 1945 to promote peace and cooperation, whose Security Council has five permanent members.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Give the following about the Non-Aligned Movement, an organization of countries interested in protecting their interests against both the Soviet-dominated Warsaw Pact and the US-dominated NATO, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: The concept of non-alignment was developed by diplomats during discussions in this international body, as countries like India and Yugoslavia refused to contribute to this body’s effort to help South Korea during the Korean War. The US is one of five permanent members of this global body’s Security Council.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Non-Aligned Movement grew out of the Bandung Conference, a 1955 meeting hosted by President Sukarno on this country’s island of Java.
parts.answer: Indonesia (accept Republic of Indonesia; accept Republik Indonesia)

parts.label: C
parts.question: The Non-Aligned Movement was co-founded by, among other leaders, this President of Egypt who led from 1956 to 1970.
parts.answer: Gamal Abdel Nasser (accept Jamal ‘Abd al-Nasir; accept Gamal Abdel Nasser Hussein)

topics.description: An anti-colonial rebellion in British Kenya led by fighters including Dedan Kimathi and General China during the 1950s.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The use of mass internment in response to this rebellion is discussed in Caroline Elkins’ 2005 book Imperial Reckoning. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this event that saw the Land and Freedom Army fight against British rule under the leadership of Dedan Kimathi and General China. The Kapenguria Six were put on trial for being the purported ringleaders of this event.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The Mau Mau uprising took place in this east African country. Many British colonists settled in this country’s capital of Nairobi during the colonial period.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] This Ugandan dictator participated in the Mau Mau uprising as an officer in the King’s African Rifles. This dictator was forced out of power after a failed invasion of Tanzania in the Kagera War.

topics.description: An ecclesiastical tribunal established by Ferdinand II of Aragon and Isabella I of Castile in 1478 to investigate and punish heresy, especially among converts from Judaism and Islam.
aliases: Tribunal of the Holy Office of the Inquisition

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Henry Kamen argued that this organization’s role behind revolts like the Alpujarras War was exaggerated as part of the “Black Legend.” The murder of Peter of Arbués led this organization to adopt new tactics against the alumbrados. This organization forced people to wear yellow sackcloths called sanbenito at public auto-da-fé’s put on by its first leader Tomás de (*) Torquemada. Following the Alhambra Decree, this organization oversaw the conversion of conversos and moriscos and the expulsion of Sephardic Jews. Ferdinand and Isabella created, for 10 points, what authoritarian religious organization that converted Spanish heretics?
parts.answer: Spanish Inquisition [or Tribunal of the Holy Office of the Inquisition]

topics.description: A 1932 Australian military operation in Western Australia that unsuccessfully attempted to control crop-damaging emus with machine guns.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Give the following about the myriad ways that western colonization of Australia ruined things, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: Most obviously, colonizers sought to assimilate or remove these indigenous people of mainland Australia.

parts.label: B
parts.question: In 1859, Thomas Austin released 24 of these animals into Australia, assuming they could do little harm; they had no predators and bred very quickly. Within 50 years, Western Australia started building a 2,000-mile-long fence meant to keep these creatures out.

parts.label: C
parts.question: In 1932, Western Australia deployed machine gunners to deal with these flightless birds. The attempts didn’t really prevent farm losses, so Australia infamously lost the “War” against these birds.

topics.description: Enslaved people were individuals subjected to chattel slavery, including Africans forcibly transported across the Atlantic during the Middle Passage.
aliases: People Enslaved in the Atlantic Slave Trade

parts.label: L
parts.question: In one novel, this author described “men without skin” who push “the woman with my face” into the sea in a stream-of-consciousness description of the Middle Passage. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this author. Another novel by this author begins with a passage from “Dick and Jane” which is repeated without punctuation and then again without spaces.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Morrison used corrupted Dick and Jane quotes as chapter headings in this 1970 novel. At the end of this novel, Soaphead Church tricks Pecola Breedlove into poisoning a dog to convince her that she has the title feature.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Morrison also wrote Beloved, which is about an escaped one of these people who kills her baby before she is recaptured. Robert Hayden’s poem “Middle Passage” describes a journey these people were forced to undertake.
parts.answer: slaves [or enslaved people; prompt on Africans or African-Americans or Black people]

topics.description: The 1948–1949 Western operation that supplied West Berlin by air during the Soviet blockade of the city.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Lucius Clay organized Operation Vittles to deliver supplies to a portion of this city. Checkpoint Charlie was the best-known location for crossing a structure in this city. A two-year Soviet blockade of this city was countered by its namesake (*) “Airlift.” Ronald Regan asked Mikhail Gorbachev to “tear down” a structure in this city. For 10 points, a wall separated the capitalist West from the communist East portion of what German capital?
parts.answer: Berlin [accept Berlin Airlift or Berlin Wall] <European History–Kapadia>

topics.description: The 1709 battle in which Peter the Great’s Russian army decisively defeated Charles XII’s Swedish forces during the Great Northern War.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The brutal occupation of one region during this war was known as the “Greater Wrath.” Johann Patkul was executed by one side in this war for treason. The Treaty of Altranstädt resulted in Augustus the Strong losing his throne in the middle of this war. The king of one side in this war was killed during the Siege of (*) Fredriksten. That king’s forces had earlier defeated an army four times their size at the Battle of Narva. The Treaty of Nystad ended this war, during which Charles XII’s forces were defeated at the Battle of Poltava. For 10 points, name this war in which Russia and its allies decisively defeated the Swedish Empire.
